# **1\. Website Strategy**

| Core goal Help a parent quickly understand what Meu Labs does, decide where their child should start, and complete registration for a relevant intake. When the parent is unsure, route them to a student counselor who can guide them to the correct course registration link. |
| :---- |

## **1.1 Target audiences**

| Audience | What they need | Website response |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Parents of ages 8–12 | A safe, beginner-friendly starting point. | Promote Knowledge Explorers as the easiest first step. |
| Parents of ages 10–14 | A way to choose between interests like data, making, and creative technology. | Use a course chooser and clear pathway cards. |
| Older students / parents of teens | Advanced STEM skills that feel serious and future-ready. | Highlight DS/AI and SE as specializations with outcomes and capstones. |
| Unsure parents | Human guidance without needing to read every page. | Use “Talk to a Student Counselor” CTAs that open WhatsApp or show a phone number. |
| School / partner stakeholders | Credibility, outcomes, and delivery model confidence. | Place partnership credibility content in About for MVP. |

## **1.2 Success metrics**

* Course page visits from the homepage and Courses page.  
* Registration button clicks per course and per intake card.  
* WhatsApp counselor clicks from uncertain-parent CTAs.  
* Phone call clicks from Contact page.  
* Project gallery engagement, especially clicks from projects to related courses.  
* Reduced repeated parent questions about age fit, course pathway, duration and next intake.

## **1.3 Writing principles**

* Every major page should answer one parent question clearly.  
* Every course page should end with registration options plus a counselor fallback.  
* Use parent-friendly wording: “course”, “child”, “starting point”, “next intake”, “builds”, “projects”.  
* Avoid making parents understand internal curriculum logic before they can take action.  
* Keep advanced details available, but make the main CTA obvious.

# **2\. Sitemap & User Flows**

## **2.1 MVP sitemap**

| Route | Page name | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| / | Home | Explain Meu Labs, show the pathway, and route parents to Courses or Contact. |
| /projects | Projects | Show proof through student work and route users to related courses. |
| /courses | Courses | Help parents compare options and choose the right course. |
| /courses/kx | Knowledge Explorers | Course page with KX content and KX registration cards. |
| /courses/an | Analytics | Course page with AN content and AN registration cards. |
| /courses/pd | Product Design | Course page with PD content and PD registration cards. |
| /courses/cx | Creative Expression | Course page with CX content and CX registration cards. |
| /courses/se | Software Engineering | Course page with SE content and SE registration cards. |
| /courses/ds | Data Science & AI | Course page with DS/AI content and DS/AI registration cards. |
| /contact | Contact / Student Counselor | WhatsApp and call flow for unsure parents. |
| /about | About | Credibility, learning model, partner proof, and outcomes. |

## **2.2 Main conversion flow**

1. Parent lands on the homepage.  
2. Parent understands that Meu Labs teaches project-based robotics, coding, design, data and AI.  
3. Parent clicks “Explore Courses” or a course card.  
4. Parent lands on a course page and checks age fit, projects, outcomes and structure.  
5. Parent scrolls to the registration section and selects an intake.  
6. Registration link opens the relevant form or payment flow.

## **2.3 Unsure parent / counselor flow**

7. Parent clicks “Help Me Choose” or “Talk to a Student Counselor”.  
8. Contact page opens with WhatsApp and phone options.  
9. WhatsApp opens with a pre-filled message.  
10. Student counselor asks child age, interests, experience and preferred schedule.  
11. Counselor recommends one course and sends the relevant course registration link.

| Important flow rule Every path should eventually lead to one of the course-specific registration links. Contact should support conversion, not replace it. |
| :---- |

# **3\. Shared Design System**

## **3.1 Visual direction**

* Modern, warm, parent-friendly and credible. Avoid looking like a generic tuition site.  
* Use large rounded cards, soft shadows, white/glass panels, and generous spacing.  
* Use real student/project imagery wherever possible to build trust.  
* Use orange for primary CTAs, navy for credibility and headings, and light backgrounds for warmth.

## **3.2 Suggested core UI tokens**

| Token | Value / direction | Usage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Primary navy | \#0D3557 | Headings, nav text, footer, trust sections. |
| Primary orange | \#FF7A00 | Primary CTA buttons, highlights, course accents. |
| Soft cream | \#FFF6EA / \#F8F1E2 | Page backgrounds and warm sections. |
| Sky blue | \#1995D3 | Secondary cards, course accents, info chips. |
| Teal | \#2CAC95 | Success/progression highlights. |
| Typography | A clean sans-serif such as Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans, or Aptos-style web font. | Use big display headings with readable body text. |

## **3.3 Global navigation**

| NAV ITEMS Home Courses Projects About Contact |
| :---- |

* Primary CTA in nav: “Explore Courses” or “Book / Register”.  
* On mobile, use a simple menu with Course links clearly visible.  
* Avoid too many top-level pages during MVP. Keep advanced credibility pages inside About for now.

## **4.1 Course card component**

| Field | Example | UI note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Course title | Knowledge Explorers | Large heading. |
| Age range | Ages 8–12 | Use it as a chip near the top. |
| Short description | Start here for hands-on robotics, coding, and STEM foundations. | 2 lines maximum on cards. |
| Pathway stage | Foundations / Learning Path / Specialization | Can use color-coded tag. |
| Key Words | Coding, Robotics, STEM | These can be something like a chip |
| CTA | Register Now | Explore Course | Always links to the course detail page which will also have the registration details |

## **4.3 Counselor CTA component**

| STANDARD COPY Not sure where your child should start? Talk to a Meu Labs student counselor and we’ll help you choose the best course based on your child’s age, interests and experience level. CTA: Talk to a Student Counselor Secondary CTA: View All Courses |
| :---- |

* Use this component on Home, Courses, every Course page, and Contact.  
* On click, either route to /contact or open WhatsApp directly depending on page context.  
* Use a pre-filled WhatsApp message with course context when possible.

## **4.4 Registration card component**

![][image2]

Reference pattern: compact intake cards with date, time, scarcity, closing date and register CTA.

| Field | Example copy | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Section title | Upcoming Intakes | Appears near the end of every course page. |
| Subtitle | Choose a batch and register for the intake that works best for your child. | Keep simple and parent-friendly. |
| Card label | Weekend Batch / Evening Batch / Morning Batch | Use batch type or location, not internal class code only. |
| Start date | Starts May 25 | Make it clear this is the first class date. |
| Time | Saturdays, 2:00pm – 5:00pm | Include day and time together. |
| Location | Meu Labs Colombo 06 | Add online/physical if relevant. |
| Availability | 4 spots left | Optional; only show if data is reliable. |
| Registration close | Registration closes May 20 | Avoid live countdowns unless maintained properly. |
| CTA | Register Now → | Links to that specific intake registration form. |

## **6.3 Featured Projects**

| EXACT DRAFT COPY Eyebrow: Featured Projects Title: Standout projects from the Meu Labs community Project Card content  Rain Sensor Link: [https://youtu.be/kq\_oZhAgNT4](https://youtu.be/kq_oZhAgNT4) A young Meu Labs student built a rainfall detection system using a water sensor, buzzer, LEDs, LCD display, and Arduino board. When the sensor detects rain, the system alerts users with a blinking red LED and buzzer. When the surface becomes dry again, the alert turns off and a white LED indicates normal conditions. This project shows how simple electronics and sensors can be used to create practical weather-monitoring tools. Dragon Ball Z Game Link: [https://youtu.be/jNGwXJ68ofI](https://youtu.be/jNGwXJ68ofI) A Meu Labs learner created a Scratch game inspired by a favourite animated series. Through this project, the student explored game design, character control, animation, and block-based programming. The project reflects both creativity and growing confidence in turning personal interests into interactive digital experiences. Home Automation System Link: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wuo9nqrSFM8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wuo9nqrSFM8) A Meu Labs student developed a smart home automation system that can be controlled through Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. The project includes a relay system, LED lights, and a mobile application built using MIT App Inventor. By combining electronics, app development, and wireless control, the student created a practical IoT system that demonstrates how technology can make everyday spaces smarter. DIY Power Generator Link: [https://youtu.be/1hEFNYY8peE](https://youtu.be/1hEFNYY8peE) A Meu Labs learner built a DIY power generator using rotating DC motors to produce electricity through electromagnetic induction. This project helped the student explore how motion can be converted into electrical energy, connecting physics concepts with a working hands-on prototype. It is a strong example of learning engineering through experimentation and making. Voice Controlled Rover Link: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=99eoCu-d6z0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=99eoCu-d6z0) A Meu Labs student built a rover that can be controlled using voice commands. The project uses an Arduino board and Bluetooth module to receive commands and control movement wirelessly. By combining robotics, electronics, programming, and communication systems, the student created an interactive robot that responds to human input in real time.  |

## **7.3 FAQ section**

| Question | Draft answer |
| :---- | :---- |
| Which course should my child start with? | If your child is new to robotics, coding or STEM, Knowledge Explorers is usually the best starting point. If they already have experience or a strong interest, our student counselors can help recommend the right course. |
| Can my child join without prior experience? | Yes. Several Meu Labs courses are designed for beginners. Advanced specializations may require prior learning or instructor guidance before joining. |
| How are classes delivered? | Most Meu Labs courses are delivered through weekly guided sessions with hands-on projects, instructor support and structured learning outcomes. |
| What happens after one course? | Students can continue along the Meu Labs pathway into learning paths and advanced specializations based on their interests and readiness. |

# **12\. Developer Handoff Checklist**

## **12.1 Recommended technical setup**

* Use Next.js with a reusable route structure and component-based course pages.  
* Use Tailwind or a similar utility-first design system for consistent spacing and cards.  
* Connect GitHub to Vercel so each pull request gets a preview deployment.  
* Store course data in one central file at MVP stage. Move to a CMS later only if needed.  
* Use environment variables for WhatsApp numbers, analytics IDs and form URLs where possible.

## **12.2 Suggested data files**

| File | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| courses.ts | All course content, slugs, age ranges, outcomes, projects and progression. |
| intakes.ts | Course-specific batch/intake data and registration links. |
| projects.ts | Student project gallery cards and related course links. |
| siteConfig.ts | Phone number, WhatsApp number, address, social links and global CTA settings. |
| faqs.ts | Shared FAQs for course pages and Courses page. |

## **12.3 Suggested component list**

* Header / Navbar  
* Footer  
* HeroSection  
* CourseCard  
* PathwayCard  
* ProjectCard  
* RegistrationSection  
* RegistrationCard  
* CounselorCTA  
* FAQAccordion  
* WhatsAppButton  
* InfoChips  
* SectionHeader

## **12.4 Analytics events to track**

| Event | Triggered when |
| :---- | :---- |
| course\_card\_click | User clicks a course card from Home or Courses. |
| registration\_click | User clicks Register Now on an intake card. |
| whatsapp\_click | User opens WhatsApp from any CTA. |
| call\_click | User taps phone number on Contact. |
| project\_card\_click | User clicks a project card or related course link. |
| help\_me\_choose\_click | User clicks a counselor CTA. |

## **12.5 Content placeholders to confirm before build**

* Final WhatsApp number and phone number.  
* Final registration links for each course and intake.  
* Current course durations, fees, schedules and age ranges.  
* Actual student project images/videos and permission to use them.  
* Partner/school names that can be publicly listed.  
* Exact address and opening/contact hours.  
* Whether “Creative Expression” or “Creative Expressions” is the final public name.

## **12.6 MVP build sequence**

12. Set up Next.js project, design tokens and global layout.  
13. Build reusable components: hero, cards, CTAs, registration cards and footer.  
14. Create Home, Courses and Course Page Template first.  
15. Add course-specific content from courses.ts.  
16. Build Projects, Contact and About pages.  
17. Add real registration links and WhatsApp message links.  
18. QA mobile responsiveness, CTA routing and Vercel preview links.  
19. Review with team, edit copy, then launch MVP.

| Final note The MVP should stay focused. The website can later grow into separate credibility pages, school/partner pages, blogs and MeuNets pages — but the first version should make course choice and registration extremely clear. |
| :---- |
